english: Hey, how's everything? (enthusiastic Najdi greeting between acquaintances)
Where are you headed? (friendly casual opener used when passing someone)
I want two tickets. How much is each one?
Are there still tickets available today?
Take me to [place]... how much do you charge?

arabic: عداد الميتر بس، ما أبي سعر ثابت
transliteration: 'Addād il-mītar bas, mā abi si'r thābit
english: Meter only please, I don't want a fixed price
I want chicken kabsa without spice
Give me extra bread, and a Saudi coffee
This is expensive, come down a little for me
I'll pay cash — will you lower the price for me?
Thank you (lit. may your hands be safe) — God bless your effort (distinctly Najdi expression)
Thank you — may God prolong your life (warm Najdi farewell-thanks)
Where is the nearest roundabout? (common Riyadh navigation reference)
Turn right after the traffic lights

arabic: بعيد ولّا قريب من هنا؟ أقدر أمشي؟
transliteration: Ba'īd willa garīb min hina? Agdar amshi?
english: Is it far or close from here? Can I walk?
Welcome, how are you? (warm standard Hijazi greeting)
How are you doing? Everything OK? (casual Jeddawi check-in)
I want one ticket. How much? (bigaddaish = how much, distinctly Hijazi)

arabic: في تذاكر متوفّرة دلوقتي ولّا لا؟
transliteration: Fī tathākir mutawwaffira dilwagti willa lā?
english: Are there tickets available right now or not? (dilwagti = right now, Hijazi marker)

arabic: خذني على البلد القديم كمان تعرف الطريق؟
transliteration: Khuthni 'ala il-balad il-gadīm — kamān ti'rif iṭ-ṭarīg?
english: Take me to the old city (Al-Balad) — do you know the route?
How much from Al-Balad to the Corniche? (kamān = how much, used in Hijazi)

arabic: أبغى مطبق باللحم وبيض، بدون حار
transliteration: Abgha muṭabbag bil-laḥm wa bayd, bidōn ḥār
english: I want mutabbaq with meat and egg, not spicy
Bring me extra tamees bread and a coffee without sugar

arabic: ما يصلح كذا. قلّل شوي يا أخوي
transliteration: Mā yiṣlaḥ kithi. Gallil shway yā akhōy
english: That won't do. Lower it a bit, brother (yā akhōy = common Jeddawi appeal)
I have cash — can you give me a discount?
Thank you — God keep you safe, you're so kind (yā ṭayyib = you're good-natured, a Hijazi warmth marker)
Much appreciated — you're a delight (lit. 'you lived and we enjoyed ourselves,' idiomatic Hijazi gratitude)
Where is the Corniche from here? (fain/fayn = where, Hijazi usage vs Najdi 'wain')
Turn left at the second traffic light (liff = turn, common Hijazi directional verb)

arabic: قريب تمشي ولّا بعيد نروح بالسيارة؟
transliteration: Garīb tamshi willa ba'īd nrūḥ bis-sayyāra?
english: Is it close enough to walk, or far enough we need to drive?
